subject: Subject: Freedom of Information Request - Ty Mawr (Great House), Llandough, near Penarth (1938-1987)
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Sir/Madam,

I understand you may already be busy, so please don't feel overwhelmed by
this FOI request—I'm conducting my own diligence and happy for you to take
the full statutory 20 working days to respond.

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, I request copies of all records,
correspondence, memoranda, internal notes, minutes, file notes, land
registration applications, objections, or communications held by HM Land
Registry from 1 January 1938 to 31 December 1987 relating to:Ty Mawr (Great
House), Llandough, near Penarth, South Glamorgan (also known as Great House
Farm).

Land registration applications, title transfers, or dealings involving
Mountjoy Ltd, Western Ground Rents Ltd, BP Pension Trust Ltd, and/or BP
Properties Ltd (including the 1938 auction/reversion conveyance and 1969
sale).

Interactions, notices, proceedings, tenancy offers, licences (e.g., 1974
unilateral lifetime licence letters), or disputes involving Mrs Mary
Williams (also referred to as Mrs Buckler), Mr Frederick Buckler, or
Williams/Buckler family occupiers—particularly the 1962 Cardiff County
Court possession proceedings (Dec 11 order by Judge Temple Morris QC).

Any possession proceedings, adverse possession claims, or title objections
connected to the property (e.g., 1955 High Court, 1962 Cardiff County
Court, 1974 actions).

Please include archived, off-site, or scanned records where applicable.If
exemptions apply (e.g., Section 40 personal data), specify which and why.
If costs exceed the appropriate limit, advise how to refine (e.g.,
prioritize 1955-1987 or 1962/1974 events).

I look forward to your response within 20 working days.

Yours faithfully,

Requester Esq. Sgt (Ret'd)
